title: Negating inputs in randomized evaluation
statement: Let $P$ be a Boolean predicate on $m$ signs, choose which inputs to negate, and let $\mu\in[-1,1]^m$. The randomized value of the predicate with those inputs negated at means $\mu$ equals the randomized value of $P$ at the vector obtained by negating the corresponding coordinates of $\mu$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean predicate on a finite number $m$ of signs
A choice of whether to negate each input
Each coordinate of the real vector $\mu$ lies in $[-1,1]
